title: Block
description: One block, the only kind of thing fw stores. An entry is a block too: the store keeps every block side by side in the `blocks` array of freewrites.json, and a top-level one (an entry) marks itself with `entry`; a child has no mark, its parent lists it. Fields marked readOnly are managed by fw; the rest (except content, which is the editor body) are editable fields in the editor header (`kinds` shown by name, and applied when you leave its field).

id.description: Stable unique identifier. Format: <YYYYMMDDThhmmss>-<4 hex chars>, derived from the creation time plus a random suffix. Sortable by creation order.

title.description: The block's title, written by you, or null. When null, a title derived from the first real line of its text stands in wherever one is shown (it is computed on display, never stored). Written titles are unique: `fw <title>` opens the entry by its title.

entry.description: Marks a top-level block: an entry, listed on home and kept alive with every block it reaches. Absent on a child block (its parent's content lists it).

content.description: What the block is, one of six shapes: Text (a string, may contain newlines); Paraphrase (your own words about another block, `paraphrase` naming it and `text` the words, a string like Text's: drawn as text, not live, unlike a quote; it keeps nothing alive, and one of a block that's gone is just text; a paraphrase is always inside a pericope, never one itself); Blocks (its children, by id, in order); Quote (a live view of another block, `quote` naming it; an optional `mask` of anchors into that block's text, in open/close pairs, shows only what's between them, the rest as …; an optional `show` lists which of its properties the quote's top line shows; an optional `inner` masks the quotes inside it, seen through it; an optional `lock` keeps anyone writing through it); or Image (one picture: `image` names its file in the `images` folder beside the store, named by a hash of its bytes); or Kind (what a block can be, as a poem or a to-do: `kind` its short name, `blocks` its description, child blocks held as Blocks holds them; a kind is always an entry). An entry with nothing written is empty Blocks.

mask.description: What the quote shows of each block of its target, by block id, like a block's links: spans [start, end] of that block's own text (a quote inside it is one place: [[0, 1]] when it shows). A block it doesn't list shows nothing. An empty span [p, p] shows nothing: it is where shown text was all deleted, kept so text typed there shows again. No `mask` shows it all. (In memory fw works with it as anchors into the target's whole text.)

show.description: Which of the quoted block's properties the quote's top line shows, e.g. ["title", "created"]. None, or no `show`, leaves it a plain line.

inner.description: Masks of the quotes inside what this quote shows, seen through it, by quote id: each shaped like `mask`, per block of that quote's target. Each only narrows what that quote shows (the two masks intersect).

lock.description: No writing through this quote: what it shows (and everything shown through it, at any depth) can be read, selected, copied and opened, but not changed from here. It belongs to this quote, not its source: other quotes of it, and its source opened, stay writable. Its own mask, top line and lock stay its holder's to change. Absent: unlocked. Managed by fw: Lock writing through / Unlock writing through.

image.description: The picture's file in the images folder: a hash of its bytes, then its format.

kind.description: Its name, short (`poem`, `to-do`): unique among kinds, case aside; what the header's kinds field and the search know it by.

blocks.description: Its description: its children, by id, in order, as a Blocks block's.

words.description: Word count of everything the block shows: its text, or its children's, with what it quotes flattened in (only the shown part of a masked quote; each block counted once, so loops end). Kept in sync on every edit; the editor header shows it live while writing.

created.description: When the block was first created. ISO 8601 with timezone offset, e.g. 2026-09-05T10:23:36-04:00.

updated.description: When the block last changed: its title or content, or a block inside it (not what it quotes: that text lives in its source, and a quote's anchors moving along with an edit there isn't a change). Set by fw on every save; an undo puts back the time it had. ISO 8601 with timezone offset.

links.description: Hyperlinks on a block of text: each a span of its text, `at` [start, end] (offsets into the text), pointing at an entry, `to`. Just a pointer: the entry it names isn't kept alive by it, and deleting that entry drops the link. The span moves with edits around it, grows with typing inside it, and shrinks as its text is deleted (to nothing, kept, so retyping or an undo brings it back). Each carries `created`, when it was made (links made before schema v13 have none). Managed by fw: made and removed with Link to an entry / Remove link.

created.description: When the link was made. ISO 8601 with timezone offset.

kinds.description: What the pericope is, as you said (only a pericope has kinds: a block inside one has none, and loses any it's given, as when it's moved in): each kind (a Kind block, by id) it is (true) or isn't (false); only your answers (a model's guesses are worked out apart, never stored). A block can be several kinds. Just a pointer: it keeps nothing alive, and deleting a kind drops it here. Written in the header's kinds field by name ("poem, not letter"; a new name makes a new kind).

visits.description: When the block was visited: stretches of attention on it, each ending after 10 minutes without any. Kept by fw, never an edit (it doesn't change `updated`, nor make the block count as changed). `recent` holds the last 10, oldest first, each [the minute it began (minutes since the epoch), flags]: o it was the pericope opened (home, `fw <title>`, Open it, back along the trail), c the cursor stayed in it (a few seconds, or typing), w something was written in it, q it happened through a quote. A visit to a block counts for each block it's part of, up to its entry (as `updated` does; not through quotes). `total` counts every visit, `first` is the minute of the first. Absent until its first visit (blocks from before schema v15 have none).
